calls.title: Luke/Kari
calls.summary: The team convened to discuss user interface experimentation, particularly testing inline editing methods for descriptions, highlighted by Luke Sonnet's proposal. While inline editing is seen as a fun experiment, Kari Kay raised concerns about its clunky appearance and potential layout shifts. The importance of UI consistency was emphasized to avoid degrading user experience. Technical issues with button and layout sizing were noted, particularly a height difference affecting the inline editing approach. Future refinements included a suggestion by Kari to simplify the interface by replacing the 'add description' line with a clickable link. Additionally, the team explored tech stack visualization, identifying main warehouses and SDKs, while affirming the need for expert feedback to finalize these visual depictions.
calls.keywords: Description Editing, Modal vs Inline UI, User Experience (UX), Tech Stack Visualization, SDK Languages, Data Warehouse Integration
calls.action_items:

Experiment with shorter description text UI and test removing extra lines while maintaining modal editing for descriptions (12:33)

**Kari Kay**
Draft proposed typical tech stack combinations and logos for Jeremy’s review and corrections (18:06)
Reach out to Jeremy, Graham, or Bryce for expert input on common SDK, warehouse, and tracker combinations (17:55)

calls.title: Luke / Kari Experiment Creation Flow
calls.summary: The team discussed the need for a redesign of the experiment creation and configuration workflow to enhance scalability and facilitate incremental progress. Luke Sonnet emphasized the importance of phased deliveries, as per Jeremy's direction, allowing for iterative improvements. Kari Kay highlighted concerns regarding the complexity of the current experiment detail page, advocating for the removal of outdated fields to improve user clarity and workflow efficiency. Incomplete customer insights also emerged as a challenge affecting design decisions. The proposal for modularization of setup features was introduced to provide organizations with customizable options. A two-week timeline was established for initial progress on the overview page redesign, with a clear focus on coordination with engineering for environment changes.
calls.keywords: Experiment creation, modular setup, variation-feature linkage, power calculation, draft states, overview page
